# Cervical Cancer

The National Cervical Screening Program invites women and people with a cervix aged 25 to 74 to have a Cervical Screening Test every five years. Since July 2022 everyone eligible can choose to collect their own sample. This page shows coverage, the number of tests, the uptake of self-collection and the time to colposcopy after a higher-risk result.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset .focus-areas}

## Coverage

:::: focus-area
::: focus-text
::: key-insight
[Key insight]{.insight-tag}

[`r key_figure("cervical_coverage")`]{.insight-value}

coverage rate over the 5-year reporting period among eligible people aged 25-74 in `r latest_period("cervical_coverage")`.

```{r}
sparkline("cervical_coverage")
```
:::

```{r}
insight_cards("cervical_coverage")
```

### Interpretation

Coverage is lowest among people aged 25-29 and those in their 70s, and highest in the middle age groups. Regional LGAs tend to sit below the Victorian rate.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Technical notes

1. **Coverage** is the number of people who had at least one Cervical Screening Test in the 5-year period divided by the estimated eligible population aged 25-74.
2. Five-year periods match the recommended screening interval.
3. Rates are not age-standardised.
4. **All values on this page are synthetic.** They were generated for a training exercise and must not be used for any other purpose.
:::

`r download_link("cervical_coverage")`
:::

::: focus-chart
```{r}
chart_panel("cervical_coverage")
```
:::

## Screening numbers

:::: focus-area
::: focus-text
::: key-insight
[Key insight]{.insight-tag}

[`r key_figure("cervical_screening")`]{.insight-value}

cervical screening tests among eligible people aged 25-74 were performed in `r latest_period("cervical_screening")`.

```{r}
sparkline("cervical_screening")
```
:::

```{r}
insight_cards("cervical_screening")
```

### Interpretation

Test numbers fell in 2020 and 2021 and have recovered since. Because the screening interval is five years, annual numbers also move with the cycle of people falling due.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Technical notes

1. **Screening numbers** count Cervical Screening Tests (clinician-collected and self-collected) performed in the calendar year for people aged 25-74.
2. Follow-up and diagnostic tests are excluded.
3. **All values on this page are synthetic.**
:::

`r download_link("cervical_screening")`
:::

::: focus-chart
```{r}

```

## Self-collection

:::: focus-area
::: focus-text
::: key-insight
[Key insight]{.insight-tag}

[`r key_figure("cervical_selfcollection")`]{.insight-value}

of cervical screening tests among eligible people aged 25-74 were self-collected in `r latest_period("cervical_selfcollection")`.

```{r}
sparkline("cervical_selfcollection")
```
:::

```{r}
insight_cards("cervical_selfcollection")
```

### Interpretation

Self-collection was rare until July 2022, when it became available to everyone eligible for screening. Since then it has grown quickly and now accounts for about a third of all tests. Uptake varies considerably between LGAs; the Variation view shows which areas differ from the Victorian share by more than chance.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Technical notes

1. **Self-collection rate** is the number of Cervical Screening Tests where the person collected their own vaginal sample, divided by all Cervical Screening Tests in the calendar year.
2. The downloadable table includes the number of self-collected tests as the numerator.
3. Data start in 2018, after the renewed program began in December 2017.
4. **All values on this page are synthetic.**
:::

`r download_link("cervical_selfcollection")`
:::

::: focus-chart
```{r}
chart_panel("cervical_selfcollection")
```
:::
::::

## Time to colposcopy

:::: focus-area
::: focus-text
::: key-insight
[Key insight]{.insight-tag}

[`r key_figure("cervical_colposcopy")`]{.insight-value}

of participants proceeded to colposcopy within 3 months following a screening test result with a higher risk classification in `r latest_period("cervical_colposcopy")`.

```{r}
sparkline("cervical_colposcopy")
```
:::

```{r}
insight_cards("cervical_colposcopy")
```

### Interpretation

Timeliness dipped during 2020 and 2021 and has improved gradually since. Many LGAs have small numbers of higher-risk results each year, so their rates move around a lot. The funnel plot in the Variation view separates genuine differences from that noise.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Technical notes

1. **Time to colposcopy** is the proportion of people with a higher-risk screening result who had a colposcopy within 3 months of the result.
2. The denominator is people with a higher-risk result in the calendar year.
3. **All values on this page are synthetic.**
:::

`r download_link("cervical_colposcopy")`
:::

::: focus-chart
```{r}
chart_panel("cervical_colposcopy")
```
:::
